newsitem.title: INDIA: Canada supports India's bid to join APEC.
newsitem.headline: Canada supports India's bid to join APEC.

text.p: Canada, set to chair a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum later this year, supports India's bid for full membership in the grouping, visiting Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Friday.
"Its (India's) participation in APEC would be absolutely instrumental in making that organisation effective," Axworthy told an international business conference in Calcutta.

APEC comprises 18 economies from Asia, North America and South America which hope to achieve free regional trade by 2020. India has been seeking membership to APEC, which currently has a moratorium on new members.
"We think India clearly is a major economic and political force in Asia and in fact throughout the world," Axworthy told the Confederation of Indian Industry's annual meeting.

He said the APEC summit, set for November in Vancouver, was expected to establish guidelines for the admission of new members, and Canada hoped that New Delhi's bid would be taken up under the new criteria.
"I can assure you it is very uppermost in our minds," Axworthy said, adding that he would discuss the matter with Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral during his visit.

Last month, during an official visit to India, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad poured cold water on New Delhi's hopes of quick entry into APEC, saying the grouping would become unwieldy if more nations were to join.
Axworthy was in India until January 14 to promote Canada-India economic ties and bilateral cooperation.
He was due to visit Chandigarh city in the northern state of Punjab next week to open a Canadian office to facilitate trade and the processing of visa applications in that region.
